relevance.rationale: Shows the set of cusp shapes of hyperbolic tunnel-number-one manifolds is dense in the Teichmuller space of the torus (Thm 1.1), with the analogue for tunnel number n (Thm 1.2), and consequences for exceptional Dehn fillings. Its value here is definitional rather than theorem-level: the corpus uses 'cusp shape' load-bearingly and without any source. prop:cusp-shape-bar-parity asserts the cusp shape of the figure-eight is a primitive sixth root of unity and splits it under the bar-involution; rem:winding-lattice-norm-form then builds a cusp lattice Z<1, omega> on that value, and rem:meridian-holonomy-boost hangs the meridian holonomy off it. Under the standard definition used here -- the similarity class of the Euclidean torus induced on the cusp cross-section, a point of Teichmuller space -- e^{i pi/3} is the shape of the equilateral triangles tiling that cross-section (the ideal regular tetrahedron parameter), which is not obviously the same object as the meridian-longitude modulus of the cusp torus. That is a discrepancy worth resolving before more weight is put on the cusp lattice, and it is why the proposed action is a remark pinning the definition, not a citation asserting agreement.

keyResults.locator: sec. 3 ("Recall that the Teichmuller space of the torus is the space of similarity classes...") + Def. 2.1-2.4
keyResults.statement: The cusp shape of a hyperbolic 3-manifold with torus boundary is the similarity class of the Euclidean structure induced on a neighbourhood of that boundary, i.e. a point of the Teichmuller space of the torus.
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the standard definition for a term the corpus uses in at least three blocks with no source, and against which its value for the figure-eight should be checked.

keyResults.statement: Cusp shapes of hyperbolic tunnel-number-one manifolds are dense in the Teichmuller space of the torus.
keyResults.useForFolio: Background only: it says the cusp shape is not constrained by low tunnel number, so no structural conclusion can be drawn from a particular knot's cusp shape being special.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry, and no source anywhere in the corpus for the notion of cusp shape despite three blocks depending on it.

Pin down which object 'cusp shape' names in prop:cusp-shape-bar-parity -- the Teichmuller modulus of the cusp torus, or the ideal-tetrahedron shape parameter tiling it -- and confirm the figure-eight value against the standard one. Deliberately a remark and not aid-proof: I could not settle the numerical question in this session, and the downstream cusp lattice Z<1, omega> depends on the answer.
